Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes, while considering sentiment history.

## Example 1: Date=2023-12-20

History: Prices have been declining from ~76 to ~66 over 18 days
Sentiment: Mix of positive, zero, and one negative reading

Model forecasts: Start at ~75.29 and gradually decline to ~71.80
True outcomes: Start at ~75.36 and decline to ~62.41 (more than model predicts)

Looking at the divergence:
- At day 1: Model 75.29 vs True 75.36 (close)
- Day 5: Model 80.41 vs True 80.24 (model overestimated)
- Day 10: Model 73.32 vs True 72.06 (model was too high)
- Day 15: Model 71.90 vs True 66.90 (model significantly overestimated the decline)
- Day 18: Model 70.54 vs True 63.31 (model missed the full extent of the drop)

The model appears to under-predict the decline. It's too slow in following prices down.

## Example 2: Date=2024-06-26

History: Prices around 67-74, some volatility
Sentiment: Mix including some negative readings

Model forecasts: Start at ~67.32, gradually increasing to ~71.75
True outcomes: Start at ~67.23, increasing to ~69.96 (but less than model predicts)

Divergence:
- Day 1: Model 67.32 vs True 67.23 (close)
- Day 5: Model 71.71 vs True 70.93 (model overestimated)
- Day 10: Model 69.91 vs True 67.96 (model too high)


- Day 15: Model 67.96 vs True 66.42
- Day 18: Model 67.80 vs True 66.00
- Day 25: Model 70.52 vs True 68.58

I notice a consistent pattern of model forecasts exceeding true outcomes. The model tends to overestimate prices, particularly at day 25 where there's a significant divergence of nearly 2 points. This suggests the model struggles with accurately predicting price movements, especially as time progresses.
